purpose: Provide a page heading, navigation context, metadata and explicit actions in a responsive structural header.
behaviorProvider: Native header and heading elements, with shared Link, Button and Breadcrumb for navigation.

host: heading hierarchy and meaningful page context
async feedback and route focus handoff

requirements.statement: Render h1 by default or the requested h2/h3 and assign headingId when supplied, otherwise a generated id. The header does not automatically name an outer page landmark.
Choose headingLevel and a stable headingId appropriate to the surrounding document. Route transitions must implement any desired focus or announcement handoff; PageHeader does not focus its heading.
When back is present, render it instead of breadcrumbs, even when both are supplied. Without back, only a nonempty breadcrumb collection creates the navigation row.
A back destination with href renders the shared Link; a callback destination renders the shared Button and invokes that callback. The component does not infer browser-history navigation.
Supply working links for navigation and buttons for actions. Model loading, disabled and failure states in those supplied action controls; the header has no pending-operation state.

Optional leading content precedes the heading; description and metadata follow it; actions follow the summary in document order; children render below the main row. Optional wrappers render only for truthy slot values. A numeric zero can render as text without its wrapper, so the host must format such content intentionally.
Provide metadata with enough textual context to explain status or count and give supplied icon-only actions accessible names. Arbitrary ReactNode slots do not acquire domain meaning from the header.
The main row wraps, title and description can break long text, and the narrow breakpoint gives summary and actions full width without reordering their DOM.
Keep tabs, filters and action controls in the provided slots on their shared implementations; preserve their own state and interaction semantics across layout/theme changes.
Use page-structure tokens for header spacing, typography and icons; nested Button, Link and Breadcrumb retain their own groups. Theme changes must preserve heading dimensions and action order.

limitations: PageHeader is structural; it does not manage routing, browser history, authentication or asynchronous actions.
headingId is an identifier, not a focus API, and arbitrary content is not semantically validated.
